 BMKG: Most major cities to see light rain, thunder on Thursday
 November 19, 2026 08:52 GMT+700 
 Archive – A motorcyclist rides through heavy rain along the Cilacap-Yogyakarta highway in Kalisabuk Village, Kesugihan District, Cilacap Regency. /ANTARA/Sumarwoto. 
 Archive – A motorcyclist rides through heavy rain along the Cilacap-Yogyakarta highway in Kalisabuk Village, Kesugihan District, Cilacap Regency. /ANTARA/Sumarwoto.
 Jakarta (ANTARA) - The Indonesia's Meteorology, Climatology, and Geophysics Agency (BMKG) has issued an early warning of light, moderate to heavy rain, possibly accompanied by lightning and strong winds, in various major cities across Indonesia on Thursday.
 Quoting BMKG’s official website in Jakarta, forecaster Nazmi explained that, in general, atmospheric dynamics show potential for rain cloud formation, as well as wind slowdowns and convergence, in the Andaman Sea, the Bay of Bengal, waters north of Aceh, waters west of North Sumatra to Bengkulu, the North Natuna Sea, the Karimata Strait, and the east coast of Riau to the Riau Islands.
 These conditions can increase the potential for rain cloud growth across most of those areas.
 Therefore, the agency forecasts that several cities may experience moderate to very heavy rain accompanied by lightning and strong winds today, including Medan, Padang, Tanjung Pinang, Serang, Bandung, Semarang, Yogyakarta, Surabaya, Mataram, Pontianak, Palangka Raya, Banjarmasin, Mamuju, Manado, and Ternate.
 However, several other major cities will only see light rain, namely Banda Aceh, Pekanbaru, Jambi, Bengkulu, Palembang, Pangkal Pinang, Bandar Lampung, Jakarta, Denpasar, Kupang, Tanjung Selor, Samarinda, Makassar, Palu, Kendari, Gorontalo, Sorong, Manokwari, Nabire, Jayapura, Jayawijaya, and Merauke.
 The only major city forecast to have just cloudy conditions today is Ambon.
 On a previous occasion, BMKG urged the public to boost preparedness for hydrometeorological disasters, such as floods, flash floods, landslides, and strong winds, as the rainy season begins in various parts of Indonesia.
 “Preparedness needs to be built early and continuously, given that rainfall characteristics and potential impacts can differ in each region,” said BMKG Head Teuku Faisal Fathani in a statement in Jakarta on Wednesday (11/18).
 He stressed that preparing for the rainy season should not be done only when heavy rain occurs, but should be built through an understanding of the hazards and disaster risks in one’s own neighborhood.
